solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unattractive leaders of union given little say, ultimately

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters, taken here from union, given and little
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of say is taken

explanation.surface: A grumble that the bosses of a trade union let their members have little say in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' covers three words, not just union: 'little' belongs to the pick, and only Y comes from 'say, ultimately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something unattractive is unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Lacking education, poor aunt meets violent thug

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of aunt are knocked into a new order
violent suggests a disturbance, so the letters of thug are shaken up too

explanation.surface: An uneducated person's hard-up aunt runs into a brutal thug.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams joined by 'meets': 'poor' turns AUNT into UNTA and 'violent' turns THUG into UGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never taught anything is lacking education; the adjective describes an untrained or ignorant person.

clue.text: Governs northern city mentioned in speech

indicators.note: said out loud, so the city's name is replaced by a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, in the north of England

explanation.surface: A politician running a northern English city gets a mention in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a big city in Yorkshire, northern England; its name sounds just like the verb meaning governs.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead a country or team is to be in charge of it, so a person who governs also directs and heads it.

clue.text: Find CD finished?

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc
something finished is over

explanation.surface: A question: has the CD come to its end?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'CD finished' is wordplay pretending to be a description of a record ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to find something is to come upon it for the first time.

clue.text: Hinder troublemaker editor initially employed

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of employed is used

explanation.surface: A troublesome editor first taken on at a paper gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hinder progress is to obstruct or hamper it.

clue.text: Handwriting police officer found on shallow dish

parts.note: copper is informal British slang for a policeman
a plate is a flat, shallow dish

explanation.surface: Some handwriting is discovered by a policeman lying on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'found on' puts the first piece above the second. Copper is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: copperplate is a neat, looping style of script, named after engraved copper printing plates.

clue.text: Butterfly Virginia observed circling a loch

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the state's letters sit around the others

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Someone called Virginia watches a butterfly flying round a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed' is only a link here. 'a loch' gives A plus the name of the famous loch in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the genus of red admirals and painted ladies, a familiar group of butterflies, has this name.

clue.text: People in Derby, for example?

definitions.meaning: a people, as in an ethnic group sharing descent
the Derby is a famous English horse ... run at Epsom

explanation.surface: A question about the crowd at Derby, a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the Midlands town; it is the flat horse race run each year at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an ethnic group of humankind, and a speed contest such as the Derby.

clue.text: Eg Earl Grey's dance where refreshments are served

parts.note: Earl Grey is a kind of tea, and 's here is read as is, giving tea is, shortened to TEAS
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A historical Earl Grey's dance held at a place serving snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey looks like the nobleman; he is the bergamot-scented tea, and Earl Grey's gives TEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a small cafe offering tea, cake and light meals is a place serving refreshments.

clue.text: The same, sour, disorganised boarding school teacher

indicators.note: disorganised means put out of order, so the eleven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boarding school teacher who is always the same: sour and muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Role: at a British boarding school, the teacher in charge of a boarding house holds this title.

clue.text: Lose one's bottle, being a grass!

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage, so losing it means losing your nerve in a crisis
a genus of grasses including millet shares this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve, and 'grass' looks like the slang for an informer but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to be overcome by sudden fear, and a type of grass such as switchgrass.

clue.text: Flawed condition of a French strait and headland

parts.note: un is French for a
a sound is a narrow sea channel or strait
ness is a word for a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A defect in a French channel and a cape on its coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite sense: being unsound means weak or defective, so this noun is a state of being faulty.

clue.text: Worshipper I swindle? Not yet

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them
something not yet done will happen later

explanation.surface: A worshipper asks whether to cheat, then decides to hold off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who worships idols or adores something blindly is a worshipper.

clue.text: Monkey's glaring mistake?

definitions.meaning: a South American monkey known for its loud call
a blunder so obvious it is laughable

explanation.surface: A monkey has made a very obvious error.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as is, joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a loud-calling South American monkey, and an obvious blunder that makes people laugh.

clue.text: Active leader of revolt in Surrey town

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the town's name

parts.note: Woking is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here from revolt

explanation.surface: The man leading an uprising in a Surrey commuter town is busy.
explanation.walkthrough: Woking is a commuter town in Surrey, south-west of London; R goes in after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something active is operating or functioning, as a machine in use is.

clue.text: Posh part of hospital, quietly carried to a higher level

indicators.note: carried means held within, so the quiet letter is borne between the other pieces

parts.note: U means upper class, the British label for posh speech and manners
a ward is a section of a hospital
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone is taken quietly from a private hospital ward to an upper floor.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage; P (piano, quietly in music) goes inside U + WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: moving towards a higher position or level is moving in an ascending direction.

clue.text: Austere city's role in South Africa…

indicators.note: in puts the role inside the country's letters

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: The part a strict city played in South Africa, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as has, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ancient Greek city famed for harsh discipline gave English its word for austere living.

clue.text: Revised assessment liars appear to develop

indicators.note: to develop means to change and grow, so the letters of liars appear are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fresh look at things suggests the liars are about to come forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: a second evaluation of something is a revised judgement of its worth.

clue.text: … upset old British PM's slumber

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister; with 's added the name gives PEELS

explanation.surface: Continuing the city story: a former prime minister's rest is disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Peel was a British prime minister in the 1830s and 1840s.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: slumber is a gentler word for being asleep.

clue.text: Seabird — or wader with bit missing?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letters of bit are taken away

parts.note: a bittern is a heron-like wading bird

explanation.surface: Is this a seabird, or a wading bird with a piece absent?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seabird' is the definition; the wader is a different bird that contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a slender, fork-tailed bird of coasts, related to gulls, is a seabird.

clue.text: One of two writers getting material rejected?

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the fabric's name is read from the end

parts.note: toile is a linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: An author is supplied with cloth that is then turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The two writers are George and T S, who share this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: George, author of Middlemarch, and T S, poet of The Waste Land, share this surname.

clue.text: Again choose City trader's opening after dance

indicators.note: after puts the city and trader pieces behind the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
EC is the postcode area of the City of London, the financial district

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here from trader's

explanation.surface: A City of London trader starts things off, then picks a dance once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to vote someone back into office is to choose them for a second time.

clue.text: Raining horribly, keeping in East African

indicators.note: keeping in means holding inside, so the jumbled letters surround the compass point
horribly suggests something messed up, so the letters of raining are jumbled

explanation.surface: It is pouring with rain, so an East African stays indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges RAINING into NIGRIAN, and 'keeping in' puts E inside it. 'East African' looks like one phrase but East is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a person from a West African country is an African.

clue.text: Stimulus almost certain to overcome pressure

indicators.note: to overcome is to get on top of and enclose, so the shortened word wraps the letter
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for certain goes

parts.note: certain means sure
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: An incentive nearly guaranteed to get past the pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts SURE to SUR, and 'to overcome' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spur is something that urges a person on, an incentive or stimulus.
